primitives.name: BatchBALD Acquisition Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model BatchBALD acquisition function: mutual information between the JOINT of a batch's labels and the model parameters: a_BatchBALD({x1..x_b}, p(ω|D_train)) = I(y1..y_b; ω | x1..x_b, D_train) = H(y_{1:b} | x_{1:b}, D_train) - E_{p(ω|D_train)}[H(y_{1:b} | x_{1:b}, ω, D_train)].
primitives.latex: \mathcal{A}_{\text{BatchBALD}}(\mathcal{B}) = I(\mathbf{y}_{1:b}; \omega \mid \mathcal{B}, D_{\text{train}}) = H(\mathbf{y}_{1:b} \mid \mathcal{B}, D_{\text{train}}) - \mathbb{E}_{p(\omega \mid D_{\text{train}})}[H(\mathbf{y}_{1:b} \mid \mathcal{B}, \omega, D_{\text{train}})]

primitives.assumptions: Model parameters ω are distributed according to posterior p(ω|D_train); labels y_i are conditionally independent given ω.

reasoning_traces.think:
BatchBALD operates on the principle of joint mutual information to select informative yet diverse batches. It computes the reduction in uncertainty about model parameters ω induced by observing a batch of labels y1..yb. The key insight is that individual BALD scores (which sum marginal entropies) suffer from redundancy because they do not account for label correlations. BatchBALD instead evaluates the joint entropy H(y1..yb | x1..xb, D_train) minus expected conditional entropy E_p(ω|D_train)[H(y1..yb | x1..xb, ω, D_train)], effectively capturing how much new information a batch contributes beyond what previous selections already provide. This leads to a submodular objective that admits a (1 - 1/e) approximation via greedy selection. In GSI, this translates into robust calibration of probabilistic forecasts using Bayesian posteriors, particularly when dealing with uncertain or sparse data. For GSE, it enables efficient weekly charting cycles by minimizing redundant picks and maximizing predictive diversity within a fixed batch size, aligning with the retraining cost constraints inherent in operational systems.
